stories.headline: Neura Robotics closes Series C of up to $1.4B at ~$7B valuation, led by Tether

key_facts.fact: German humanoid robotics maker Neura Robotics announced a Series C of up to $1.4 billion, led by Tether, with participation from Nvidia, Amazon, Qualcomm, Bosch, Schaeffler, the European Investment Bank, imec.xpand, Lingotto Horizon and InterAlpen Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: 10 June 2026 - Tether Investments announced today its role as the lead investor in one of the largest private investment rounds in humanoid robotics. By supporting the raise of up to $1.4bn from a diversified group of strategic and financial investors into NEURA Robotics...

key_facts.fact: The round valued the Metzingen-based company at roughly $7 billion, according to a source familiar with the matter cited by CNBC; Neura declined to confirm the figure.
key_facts.excerpt: The company hit a valuation of around $7 billion, according to a source familiar with the matter, who asked to remain anonymous as they weren't authorized to discuss the information. The company declined to comment on the valuation.

key_facts.fact: The full $1.4 billion is contingent on Neura hitting undisclosed operational milestones; the company has not said when it expects to receive the full amount.
key_facts.excerpt: NEURA will receive the full $1.4 billion only if it meets certain undisclosed milestones, and the company has not said when it expects to receive the full amount.

key_facts.fact: Robotics companies have raised $55.8 billion globally so far in 2026, nearly double the prior year's total, per Dealroom data cited by CNBC.
key_facts.excerpt: Robotics companies have raised $55.8 billion so far in 2026, according to Dealroom.

key_facts.fact: Tether will embed its open-source Wallet Development Kit (WDK) and QVAC edge-AI runtime into Neura's robots, enabling machines to hold self-custodial wallets and execute transactions locally.
key_facts.excerpt: Beyond capital, Tether will embed its crypto wallet tech and edge AI runtime directly into NEURA's robotic systems.

key_facts.fact: Neura plans to scale serial production to several million robots by 2030 and to expand its global network of 'NEURA Gyms' — real-world training environments for cognitive robots.
key_facts.excerpt: NEURA plans to use the capital to scale serial production to several million robots by 2030 and to expand its global network of NEURA Gyms — training environments for cognitive robots in real-world deployment scenarios.

stories.headline: Applied Materials opens $500M Tampines campus, making Singapore ~50% of its global capacity

key_facts.fact: Applied Materials opened a US$500 million (S$644 million) Tampines manufacturing and R&D campus in Singapore on June 10, more than doubling its advanced cleanroom capacity in the city-state.
key_facts.excerpt: Applied Materials, Inc., the leader in materials engineering solutions for the semiconductor industry, has expanded its manufacturing and R&D operations in Singapore to support the global build-out of AI infrastructure. The new US$500 million (S$600 million) Tampines Campus more than doubles Applied's advanced cleanroom capacity in Singapore.

key_facts.fact: The new facility brings Applied Materials' Singapore sites from one to three, making the city-state home to roughly half of the company's global production capacity, with the remainder in the US.
key_facts.excerpt: The new campus increases Applied Materials' manufacturing sites in Singapore from one to three, making the city-state home to roughly half of the company's global production capacity, with the remainder located in the U.S.

key_facts.fact: Applied employs about 4,000 people in Singapore and plans to add 1,000 new local jobs over the next few years.
key_facts.excerpt: Applied Materials opened the doors of its new plant to produce chip-making machines, doubling its manufacturing footprint in Singapore and creating 1,000 new local jobs over the next few years.

key_facts.fact: CEO Gary Dickerson said more than 80% of growth in wafer fab equipment is tied to leading-edge logic, memory, and advanced packaging; Applied expects advanced packaging equipment revenue to grow 50% in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Dickerson said more than 80% of growth in wafer fab equipment is tied to leading-edge logic, memory, and advanced packaging. [...] Applied Materials expects revenue from advanced packaging equipment to increase 50% in 2026.

key_facts.fact: The campus deploys autonomous mobile robots, autonomous assembly and testing systems, and AI-assisted quality inspection.
key_facts.excerpt: Top U.S. chip equipment maker Applied Materials has opened a $500 million manufacturing campus in Singapore, the linchpin in the company's plan to nearly double its global production capacity to meet surging demand from the AI-driven chip boom.

stories.headline: Amazon signs $17.5B delayed-draw term loan led by Citigroup to fund AI buildout

key_facts.fact: Amazon disclosed a $17.5 billion senior unsecured delayed draw term loan facility led by Citibank, with JPMorgan, Bank of America, HSBC, Wells Fargo and over a dozen other banks participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon has entered into a term loan agreement with Citibank and more than a dozen other banks that provides the company with a $17.5 billion senior unsecured delayed draw term loan credit facility (DDTL Facility).

key_facts.fact: The facility is available through September 30, 2026; each draw must be repaid within three years and pays SOFR plus 0.625-0.875 percentage points depending on Amazon's credit rating.
key_facts.excerpt: The loan will pay 0.625 percentage point to 0.875 percentage point more than the Secured Overnight Financing Rate, or SOFR, with the exact amount depending on Amazon's credit rating.

key_facts.fact: The new loan comes two days after Amazon priced C$14 billion (about US$10 billion) in Canadian-dollar bonds — the largest corporate bond sale on record in that currency — bringing new financing to roughly $31.5 billion in 48 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: The loan comes just two days after it was reported that Amazon would also raise $14 billion in a Canadian bond sale, bringing its total new financing to roughly $31.5 billion in the span of roughly 48 hours.

key_facts.fact: Amazon's total short- and long-term debt (including lease payments) exceeded $225 billion as of March 31, up from roughly $150 billion a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: As of 31 March, Amazon's total short- and long-term debt, including lease payments, exceeded $225 billion. A year earlier, that figure was closer to $150 billion.

key_facts.fact: Amazon has guided to about $200 billion in capex in 2026, mainly on new data centers and chips; Q1 capex alone hit $43.2 billion, the highest among Big Tech.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has said it plans to spend approximately $200 billion in capital expenditure in 2026, mainly on new data centres and chips. Q1 spending alone hit $43.2 billion, the highest among Big Tech.

key_facts.fact: Amazon said proceeds will go to general corporate purposes including 'supporting business investments, funding future capital expenditures, and repaying debt'; analysts at CreditSights flagged the loan could help fund equity stakes in OpenAI (up to $50B) and Anthropic (up to $25B).
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg reported on the agreement Wednesday and said that an Amazon spokesperson said that the general corporate purposes for which the proceeds of the loan may be used include 'supporting business investments, funding future capital expenditures, and repaying debt.'

stories.headline: Texas Governor Abbott directs PUC and ERCOT to make data centers pay for their grid costs

key_facts.fact: Governor Greg Abbott sent a letter on June 10 directing the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) and ERCOT to require data centers to fund their own electric infrastructure so residential ratepayers do not absorb those costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Abbott's letter uses stronger language, directing the agency to 'take action to require data centers to pay for all of their electric infrastructure costs to ensure that no residential ratepayer is burdened by those costs.'

key_facts.fact: Abbott ordered the agencies to submit a memorandum by July 17 outlining actions to protect ratepayers and required the PUC to initiate action to reduce residential transmission costs by July 31.
key_facts.excerpt: Submit a memo to Abbott by July 17 with actions they can take to protect residential and small business ratepayers. For PUC, 'initiate action' to reduce residential customers' infrastructure costs by July 31.

key_facts.fact: More than 480 'large' data centers have applied to connect to the ERCOT grid through 2032; only about a dozen of those currently drawing power are classified as large users (consuming at least as much as 18,750 households).
key_facts.excerpt: More than 480 'large' data centers have requested to connect to the ERCOT grid through 2032, according to the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, the grid operator. Currently, only a dozen of the hundreds of data centers drawing power from the state's primary grid are considered 'large' electricity users, meaning they consume at least as much power as 18,750 households.

key_facts.fact: Abbott also pledged 2027 legislative priorities: codifying the cost-payment rule, requiring water-efficient cooling, mandating annual electricity and water reporting, repealing data center sales tax exemptions, and adding noise protections for neighbors.
key_facts.excerpt: The governor said he plans to 'codify' the PUCT's actions to force data centers to pay for their own electric infrastructure and contribute to the state's electric supply. Abbott also said he will work to pass legislation that will require data centers to use 'water-efficient technologies' and report their electricity and water usage; repeal financial incentives and tax exemptions for these facilities; and reduce their impact on nearby communities.

key_facts.fact: The move marks the first time the Republican governor has sought to put limits on data center growth, which has drawn backlash even in heavily GOP areas; the Texas Senate Committee on Finance will meet July 27 to discuss the sales tax exemption.
key_facts.excerpt: The Texas Senate Committee on Finance will meet July 27 at 10:30am to discuss the sales tax exemption for data centers.

stories.headline: Oracle plans $40B FY27 raise and ~$70B capex as RPO hits $638B; stock falls ~10% on capex shock

key_facts.fact: Oracle reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $19.2 billion, up 21% year-over-year, ahead of the $19.1B Street estimate; adjusted EPS of $2.11 beat the $1.97 estimate.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $19.2 billion, up 21% year on year, and adjusted earnings of $2.11 per share, beating analyst estimates of $19.1 billion and $1.97 respectively.

key_facts.fact: Remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up from $553 billion three months earlier and well above the $589.5B analyst estimate; four customers each signed deals worth more than $8 billion in the quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Remaining performance obligations, Oracle's measure of contracted future revenue, reached $638 billion at the end of the quarter, up from $553 billion three months earlier and well above the $589.5 billion analysts expected. The company said most of the new bookings were for large-scale AI contracts in which customers prepaid for expensive GPU servers.

key_facts.fact: Oracle spent roughly $55.7 billion on capex in fiscal 2026 (vs. its own $50B guidance) and expects net cash capex of about $70 billion in FY27, with reported capex $20B–$25B higher due to customer prepayments and timing.
key_facts.excerpt: The company spent approximately $55.7 billion on capital expenditure in the fiscal year ended May 31, exceeding its previous guidance of $50 billion. Oracle now expects to spend roughly $70 billion in net capital expenditure in fiscal 2027, with the reported figure $20 billion to $25 billion higher due to prepayments for components, CFO Hilary Maxson said on the earnings call.

key_facts.fact: Oracle plans to raise about $40 billion through debt and equity in fiscal 2027 — including a previously announced $20 billion at-the-market equity issuance — after raising $43B in debt and $5B in equity in FY26; it does not expect to issue additional debt in calendar 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: In fiscal year 2026, Oracle raised $43 billion in debt financing and $5 billion in equity financing. In fiscal year 2027, Oracle expects to raise approximately $40 billion through a combination of debt and equity financing including its previously announced $20 billion at-the-market equity issuance. Oracle does not expect to issue additional debt in calendar year 2026.

key_facts.fact: Prepaid and customer-supplied GPU portions of Oracle's large AI contracts now total $75 billion, which Oracle says 'substantially reduces' the capital it needs to raise for its AI data center build-out.
key_facts.excerpt: Most of the RPO increase in both Q3 and Q4 were large scale AI contracts where the customer prepaid Oracle for the purchase of the GPUs, or the customer bought and supplied the GPUs to Oracle. The prepaid and customer supplied hardware portions of our large AI contracts now total $75 billion.

key_facts.fact: ORCL stock dropped about 10% in extended trading on the FY27 capex and capital-raise outlook; co-CEO Clay Magouyrk said Oracle is bringing nearly 1 gigawatt of computing online in the current quarter, roughly matching all of fiscal 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The stock dropped 10% in extended trading as the company plans to raise more money to finance its AI buildout. [...] The company is looking to bring online almost one gigawatt worth of computing power in the current quarter, roughly the total for fiscal 2026, Oracle CEO Clay Magouyrk said on a conference call with analysts.

stories.headline: Ricursive, founded by Google AlphaChip leads, raises $335M to build an end-to-end AI chip design model

key_facts.fact: Palo Alto startup Ricursive, founded by the two leads of Google's AlphaChip project, has raised $335 million to develop an end-to-end AI model for chip design.
key_facts.excerpt: Palo Alto, Calif. — Startup Ricursive, founded by the two leads from Google's famous AlphaChip project, is aiming to develop an end-to-end AI model for chip design. The new AI frontier lab is focused on hardware workload co-optimization, with the first stages of its rollout targeting workload-specific chip design for third parties. The company has raised $335 million, which will largely be spent on GPU compute hours as it trains and tests its model.

key_facts.fact: Most of the capital will be spent on GPU compute hours to train and test the model.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has raised $335 million, which will largely be spent on GPU compute hours as it trains and tests its model.

key_facts.fact: Ricursive is rolling out in three phases: starting with workload-specific chip design services for third parties, then an end-to-end model that ingests workloads and outputs GDSII files ready for manufacturing.
key_facts.excerpt: Ricursive has planned three stages for its technology rollout. The company is currently working on phase one. In this phase, Ricursive will take on portions of chip design for chip companies, improving performance and helping companies get to market faster. Phase two will combine the stages of chip design into an end-to-end model that can ingest workloads and spit out GDSII files ready for manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: The startup trains on generally available web data and open-source chip data and can generate synthetic data; co-founder Anna Goldie argued advanced models need less data because knowledge can transfer across tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: Ricursive is training its model on generally available web data and open-source chip data, but can also create and use synthetic data to avoid hitting the limits of what is available in the real world today. Advanced AI models need less data, Goldie said, since knowledge can transfer across tasks.

stories.headline: Nvidia halves SOCAMM capacity in Vera Rubin Superchip module amid LPDDR5X memory shortage

key_facts.fact: TrendForce reported on June 10 that Nvidia has decided to halve the SOCAMM capacity for its next-generation Vera Rubin Superchip module to address anticipated LPDDR5X memory supply shortages by early 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: On June 10, 2026, TrendForce reported that NVIDIA NVDA has decided to halve the SOCAMM capacity for its next-generation Vera Rubin Superchip module. This decision comes in response to anticipated supply shortages expected by early 2027, rather than a revision of total memory demand.

key_facts.fact: Rather than reducing total memory demand, Nvidia is cutting single-chip capacity while raising module shipments — a tactic aimed at preserving market share as LPDDR5X supply tightens.
key_facts.excerpt: By reducing single-chip capacity while increasing module shipments, NVIDIA aims to strengthen its market share amid a growing demand for LPDDR5X memory, which cannot currently be met.

key_facts.fact: Vera Rubin is Nvidia's next-generation Superchip platform; the first gigawatt of Nvidia Vera Rubin systems is targeted for the second half of 2026 under its 10GW-plus letter of intent with OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: In September 2025, Nvidia and OpenAI signed a letter of intent for at least 10 gigawatts of Nvidia systems, with Nvidia committing up to $100 billion in OpenAI as capacity comes online. The first gigawatt was targeted for the second half of 2026 using Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform.
